headline: Growth continues but EPS slips on a one-off prior-year gain
summary_short: Revenue rose to $642M (+14.7% y/y, +3.1% q/q) on higher average assets under administration (+19% y/y to $1.3T) and the Stratos acquisition, while net income fell to $196M (-13.8% y/y) because Q2 2025 included a one-time $94.4M gain on the sale of Family Office Services that Q2 2026 lacks.
summary_long: Revenue growth was driven by higher average assets under administration (+19% y/y to $1.3T, cross-sales in Investment Managers) and the Stratos acquisition ($40.1M H1 revenue), partly offset by Institutional Investors client losses. Operating income rose 32.6% y/y on the revenue gain and lower consulting/vendor costs, partially offset by higher personnel costs from growth and Stratos. EBITDA and net income fell y/y only because Q2 2025 included a one-time $94.4M gain on the sale of Family Office Services (removed as a non-GAAP adjustment) — adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted EPS actually rose to $1.66 from $1.20. Cash fell to $396M on $320.7M of H1 buybacks and $126.3M of dividends paid; shareholders' equity rose to $2,500M. No forward revenue/EPS guidance appears in the 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Revenue and operating income grew on higher AUA/AUM and the Stratos acquisition; net income and EPS look down y/y only because the year-ago quarter included a one-time $94.4M gain on selling Family Office Services.

Higher assets under administration (+19% y/y to $1.3T, cross sales to alternative-investment clients) and the Stratos acquisition ($40.1M), partly offset by client losses in Institutional Investors and lower fee structures in SEI fund programs.
Total expenses grew 8% versus 15% revenue growth this quarter; gross profit expansion is arithmetic from that gap, not a specific disclosed cause.
Revenue growth outpaced expense growth; expenses rose on higher personnel costs from business growth and the Stratos acquisition, partially offset by lower consulting and outsourced-vendor costs.

The y/y decline is fully explained by the absence of a one-time $94.4M gain on the sale of the Family Office Services business that boosted Q2 2025; the company's own non-GAAP reconciliation backs this out.

Same one-time $94.4M FOS sale gain in Q2 2025 explains the y/y decline, plus higher intangible amortization from the Stratos acquisition and non-controlling interest allocation ($3.9M) not present a year ago.
Lower net income attributable to SEI drives the EPS decline; diluted share count also fell slightly (123.3M vs 127.3M) from ongoing buybacks, which is a modest offset, not the driver.
Cash fell on $320.7M of common-stock buybacks and $126.3M of dividend payments during the first six months of 2026, partly offset by $347.4M of operating cash flow.
Equity growth is the net effect of retained-earnings additions from net income against reductions for share buybacks and dividends paid; no separate cause is narrated in the filing.
